hints: Identify all three external forces acting on the block: weight $W = mg$ acting vertically downwards, normal contact force $R$ acting perpendicular to the inclined plane, and friction $F$ acting up the plane opposing motion.
Ensure each force arrow originates from or passes through the block in the correct direction.
walkthrough:
The three forces acting on the block are:
$$\text{1. Weight } W = mg \text{ acting vertically downwards}$$
$$\text{2. Normal reaction force } R \text{ acting perpendicular to and away from the inclined plane}$$
$$\text{3. Friction force } F \text{ acting parallel to and up the inclined plane opposing the downward motion}$$

ai_rubric.Drawing Free-Body Diagrams: Includes weight vertically downwards, normal reaction perpendicular to the inclined plane, and friction acting up the slope.

teacher_walkthrough: To draw the free-body diagram for the $8\text{ kg}$ block sliding down the $30^\circ$ incline:
Weight ($W = 8g = 80\text{ N}$): drawn from the center of mass pointing vertically downwards towards the center of the Earth.
Normal reaction ($R$): drawn perpendicular to the inclined plane pointing outwards from the surface into the block.
Friction force ($F$): drawn parallel to the inclined plane pointing up the slope, opposing the direction of downward sliding.

hints: Resolve forces perpendicular to the plane to find the normal reaction: $R = 8g\cos 30^\circ = 40\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$.
Apply Newton's second law down the plane: $8g\sin 30^\circ - F = 8(2.4)$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane:
$$R = mg\cos 30^\circ = 8(10)\cos 30^\circ = 40\sqrt{3}\text{ N}\quad (\approx 69.28\text{ N})$$

Apply Newton's second law parallel to the plane down the slope:
$$mg\sin 30^\circ - F = ma$$
$$8(10)\sin 30^\circ - F = 8(2.4)$$
$$40 - F = 19.2 \implies F = 40 - 19.2 = 20.8\text{ N}$$

Calculate the coefficient of friction $\mu$ using $F = \mu R$:
$$\mu = \frac{F}{R} = \frac{20.8}{40\sqrt{3}} = \frac{13\sqrt{3}}{75} \approx 0.300$$

ai_rubric.Using Friction Relationships: Finds R = 40*sqrt(3) N, sets up 8g sin 30 - F = 8(2.4) to find F = 20.8 N, and evaluates mu = 0.300 (13*sqrt(3)/75).

teacher_walkthrough:
Resolve forces acting on the block perpendicular to the inclined plane: in this direction, there is no acceleration, so the normal reaction balances the perpendicular weight component:
$$R = mg\cos 30^\circ = (8)(10)\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 40\sqrt{3}\text{ N}\quad (\approx 69.282\text{ N})$$

Apply Newton's second law $F_{\text{net}} = ma$ parallel to the plane in the downward direction of acceleration ($a = 2.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$):
$$mg\sin 30^\circ - F = ma$$
$$(8)(10)(0.5) - F = (8)(2.4)$$
$$40 - F = 19.2$$
$$F = 40 - 19.2 = 20.8\text{ N}$$

Because the block is sliding along the rough plane, the friction force is at its limiting value $F = \mu R$:
$$\mu = \frac{F}{R} = \frac{20.8}{40\sqrt{3}}$$
$$\mu = \frac{20.8 \times \sqrt{3}}{40 \times 3} = \frac{20.8\sqrt{3}}{120} = \frac{208\sqrt{3}}{1200} = \frac{13\sqrt{3}}{75} \approx 0.30022$$
$$\mu = 0.300\quad (\text{to 3 significant figures})$$

hints: Apply the SUVAT equation $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $u = 0$, $a = 2.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $s = 3\text{ m}$.
walkthrough:
Apply the constant acceleration relation with $u = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $a = 2.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $s = 3\text{ m}$:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as$$
$$v^2 = 0 + 2(2.4)(3) = 14.4$$
$$v = \sqrt{14.4} = \frac{6\sqrt{10}}{5} \approx 3.79\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the SUVAT equation relating velocity, acceleration, and displacement:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as$$

Substitute the initial speed $u = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, acceleration $a = 2.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and distance $s = 3\text{ m}$:
$$v^2 = 0^2 + 2(2.4)(3)$$
$$v^2 = 14.4$$
$$v = \sqrt{14.4} = \sqrt{\frac{72}{5}} = \frac{6\sqrt{10}}{5} \approx 3.7947\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$v = 3.79\text{ m s}^{-1}\quad (\text{to 3 significant figures})$$
